record.paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
record.original_question: For a smooth convex curve in the plane and a possibly nonsymmetric Minkowski norm N, consider the Minkowski billiard generated by the length N(gamma(s1)-gamma(s0)), with the curve parametrized by N-arc length. If the Minkowski billiard corresponding to N inside the unit ball of N is totally integrable, must N be the Euclidean norm?

evidence.quote: Does it imply that N is Euclidean?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $N:\mathbb{R}^2\to[0,\infty)$ be a (possibly non-symmetric) Minkowski norm, i.e. a positively 1-homogeneous function that is positive on $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\}$, with smooth and strictly convex unit ball $B_N=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^2:N(x)\le 1\}$. Let $\gamma:\mathbb{R}/L\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth strictly convex closed curve, parametrized by $N$-arc length, that bounds the table $B_N$ (i.e., $\gamma$ parametrizes $\partial B_N$). Define the Minkowski billiard map on pairs $(s_0,s_1)$ via the generating function $H(s_0,s_1)=N(\gamma(s_1)-\gamma(s_0))$: trajectories are critical points of sums of $H$ along consecutive points. Say that this Minkowski billiard is totally integrable if the phase cylinder (the set of admissible $(s_0,s_1)$) is foliated by invariant curves of the billiard map that are graphs over the base.

Question: if the Minkowski billiard inside $B_N$ generated by $N$ is totally integrable, must $N$ be a Euclidean norm (i.e., $B_N$ an ellipse centered at the origin)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question (attributed in the literature to Y. Ostrover) appears to remain open in general. Partial results are known: under additional symmetry assumptions (e.g., the boundary curve being invariant under a linear map of order k ≥ 3, in particular a nontrivial finite symmetry group), total integrability of the Minkowski billiard on the entire phase cylinder forces the curve to be a circle and hence N to be Euclidean. No unconditional resolution has been located.

status_evidence.title: Integrable Billiards and Related Topics (Bialy–Mironov)
status_evidence.snippet: Rigidity results state that if a strictly convex curve invariant under a linear map of order k≥3 has totally integrable Minkowski billiard on the entire phase cylinder, then it must be a circle.
status_evidence.claim: Partial rigidity is established under symmetry hypotheses; the general question (Ostrover) is presented as open.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
status_evidence.snippet: Does it imply that N is Euclidean?
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed as an open problem in this survey.
